entities.description: Dark-soil cotton crescent of central Alabama/Mississippi; by the 19th century also the plantation-slavery and Black-majority-county region. The original referent of the term.
entities.name: Black Belt (Alabama/Southern)

entities.description: The South Side Black district as named in Chicago usage c.1900-c.1960s, with era- and source-specific boundaries; a concentration of Black residents inside a constrained housing market, never demographically uniform.
entities.name: Black Belt (Chicago)

entities.description: Sociological synonym for the segregated South Side zone, popularized by the University of Chicago school; analytic frame stressing involuntariness and pathology.
entities.name: Black Ghetto (Chicago)

entities.description: Drake and Cayton's (1945) term for the Black institutional, economic, and cultural life built inside the belt — 'the Black Belt became the Black Metropolis.'
entities.name: Black Metropolis

entities.description: 1930 Black-press coinage (James J. Gentry, Chicago Bee) adopted as the district's chosen name; a counternaming of the imposed 'Black Belt'/'Black Ghetto.'
entities.name: Bronzeville

entities.description: 24th-35th Streets, Federal-State Streets (City of Chicago landmark report).
entities.name: Chicago Black Belt, c.1890 polygon

entities.description: 22nd-39th (Wentworth-lake); 39th-55th (Clark-Michigan); contested 39th-55th (Michigan-lake). Administrative/analytic polygon from the riot commission.
entities.name: Chicago Black Belt, 1919 riot District I

entities.description: State to Cottage Grove, 31st to 47th (Chicago Urban League synthesis).
entities.name: Chicago Black Belt, 1920s working bounds

entities.description: Cermak to South Chicago Avenue, LaSalle to Lake Michigan (CUL synthesis; UIC 1940 census map).
entities.name: Chicago Black Belt, 1940s working bounds

entities.description: Titled a chapter of The Souls of Black Folk (1903) 'Of the Black Belt,' codifying the Southern term as a racial-geography label.
entities.name: W. E. B. Du Bois

entities.description: Physician and Chicago Defender columnist; 1922 column used 'Black Belt of Chicago' as ordinary vocabulary.
entities.name: Dr. A. Wilberforce Williams

entities.description: Theater editor of Anthony Overton's Chicago Bee; coined 'Bronzeville' in 1930; moved to the Defender in 1932.
entities.name: James J. Gentry

entities.description: Co-author of Black Metropolis (1945); distinguished the imposed belt/ghetto from the Black institutional metropolis.
entities.name: St. Clair Drake

entities.description: Co-author of Black Metropolis (1945).
entities.name: Horace R. Cayton

entities.description: Chicago historian (UChicago AM'54); oral-history testimony recalls growing up in the 'Black Belt' as 'a city within a city.'
entities.name: Timuel Black

entities.description: Pastor of Olivet Church; 1917/1919 source on belt overcrowding ('125,000 Negroes in quarters formerly provided for 50,000').
entities.name: Rev. L. K. Williams

entities.description: University of Chicago sociologist; Chicago School adoption of 'Black Belt' as an academic label.
entities.name: Robert E. Park

entities.description: University of Chicago sociologist; Chicago School adoption of 'Black Belt' as an academic label.
entities.name: Ernest W. Burgess

entities.description: FSA photographer; April 1941 Chicago photographs of the 'Negro section,' including the LOC-captioned 'Black Belt' apartment image.
entities.name: Russell Lee

entities.description: FSA photographer; April 1941 Chicago photograph of an apartment building subdivided into 'kitchenettes.'
entities.name: Edwin Rosskam

entities.description: Appointed after the 1919 riot; published The Negro in Chicago (Sept 1922), the strongest documentary anchor for the Chicago term and its boundaries.
entities.name: Chicago Commission on Race Relations

entities.description: Black newspaper; 1922 column used 'Black Belt of Chicago'; from 1932 promoted the 'Bronzeville' name and Mayor of Bronzeville contest.
entities.name: Chicago Defender (newspaper)

entities.description: Anthony Overton's Black newspaper; theater editor James J. Gentry coined 'Bronzeville' here in 1930; sponsored the 1930 Mayor of Bronzeville contest.
entities.name: Chicago Bee (newspaper)

entities.description: Producer of the CULtivate historical synthesis of segregation-era boundaries used for the 1920s/1940s polygons.
entities.name: Chicago Urban League

entities.description: Institutional home of Park, Burgess, Drake, and Cayton; the Chicago School carried 'Black Belt' into academic language.
entities.name: University of Chicago (sociology)

entities.description: 1903 literary codification of the Southern term as a racial-geography label.
entities.name: Publication of The Souls of Black Folk, 'Of the Black Belt'

entities.description: The violence whose investigation produced the riot-district 'Black Belt' definitions (District I) in the 1922 commission report.
entities.name: Chicago Race Riot of 1919

entities.description: September 1922 commission report; uses scare-quoted 'so-called 'Black Belt'' and multiple boundary definitions.
entities.name: Publication of The Negro in Chicago

entities.description: 1930: James J. Gentry coins the name at the Chicago Bee; Bee sponsors the Mayor of Bronzeville contest.
entities.name: Coining of 'Bronzeville'

entities.description: 1945: Drake and Cayton distinguish the imposed belt/ghetto from the Black institutional metropolis.
entities.name: Publication of Black Metropolis

entities.description: Drake and Cayton's 1945 'center of the Black Belt.'
entities.name: 47th Street and South Parkway

entities.description: Described in Dr. A. Wilberforce Williams's 1922 Defender column as in the center of Chicago's 'Black Belt' — evidence of ordinary Black-press usage.
entities.name: Michael Reese Hospital (1922)
